data_as_of: Undated scorecard data as listed by Stymie (S1) and checked against GolfPass (S2), retrieved 2026-11-10. Hazeltine does not publish its scorecard online. The Tournament-tee rating matches the 2024 U.S. Amateur fact sheet (S19). The championship course has not been changed since the 2010 greens rebuild apart from the 16th-tee project: Love Golf Design's 2029 Ryder Cup master plan was still a future phase in March 2026 (S25). Tournament setups: 2009 PGA Championship, 2016 Ryder Cup (re-routed), 2024 U.S. Amateur, 2026 KPMG Women's PGA.

greens.grass: Bentgrass. All 18 greens were rebuilt to USGA specification in summer 2010 under Rees Jones and re-grassed with bentgrass. GPS and laser surveys kept the original contours, and several greens were slightly enlarged to add hole locations (S21, S22, S23). Before the rebuild, at the 2009 PGA, they were Penncross creeping bentgrass with Poa annua (S16). The current bentgrass variety is not published.
greens.typical_stimp: 12.5-13.5 expected for the 2024 U.S. Amateur (S20). For the 2019 KPMG Women's PGA the club said speeds would be nearly identical to daily member play (S29), but no daily Stimpmeter figure is published.
greens.notes: No average or per-hole green sizes published; Golf Digest calls them 'good-size targets' (S17). Tiered or shelved greens: 1 (three tiers), 4 (two tiers with a back shelf), 10 (ridge), 17 (bowl and shelves) and 18 (three tiers). Flashed-up greenside bunkers throughout (S24).

boundaries.ob_summary: OB is documented on only two holes: No. 14, where it lines the right side and lies right of the green (S5, S18), and No. 5, where the club says OB is possible left of the fairway (S6). No local-rules sheet or white-stake map was found, so OB on the other 16 holes is unknown (null), not confirmed absent.
boundaries.penalty_area_summary: Hazeltine Lake borders the back nine. It lies left of and behind the 10th green and runs down the right of the 16th, where the drive carries it and the green sits on a peninsula; a creek runs down the left of the 16th fairway. Ponds guard the greens on 6 (front-left), 7 (left), 8 (front and right) and 13 (left), and water sits left of and around the 17th green. At championships the 8th's water has no lateral relief option, and the 17th's left-side water is described as a lateral hazard (S7). No water is described on 1-5, 9, 11, 12, 14, 15 or 18. Red/yellow marking for daily play is not published.

A new fairway built in 1977 removed a 90-degree dogleg right (S18). Fairway bunkers were added on the left of the landing area (S11). It was the easiest hole at the 2002 and 2009 PGA Championships (S31). Tournament setups: 2009 PGA Championship 572 (S15); 2016 Ryder Cup 572, played as Ryder Cup No. 16 (S12, S6); 2024 U.S. Amateur 568 (S19); 2026 KPMG Women's PGA 516 (S9). Women's handicap 3 (S2).

A new tee for 2009 stretched it to 642 and brought those bunkers back into play (S16). The original tee was a 100-yd 'runway' (S24). Tournament setups: 2009 PGA Championship 642 (S15); 2016 Ryder Cup 642, played as Ryder Cup No. 6 (S12, S6); 2024 U.S. Amateur 642 (S19); 2026 KPMG Women's PGA 530 (S9). Women's handicap 10 (S2).

penalty_areas.description: Hazeltine Lake runs down the right, and the tee shot must carry it: 200+ yd from the championship tee (S6), about 220 yd (S15), and 150-200 yd from the members' back tees after the tee rebuild (S8). A creek runs down the left of the fairway (S5, S9). The peninsula green is surrounded by the lake, and hole locations on the right bring it into play (S9, S5).

green.features: Narrow, elevated peninsula green that angles away and is hard to hold (S5, S9, S11). It is the only hole on the course without a bunker (S24, S17).

holes.notes: Signature hole; carts are not allowed on its fairway (S35). It was a 214-220 yd par 3 until it was converted to a par 4 after the 1970 U.S. Open; the old green was bulldozed into the lake to form the peninsula, and the new hole was first played publicly at the 1983 U.S. Senior Open (S8, S18, S19). It was lengthened 18 yd after 1991 (S8). Rees Jones later moved the tees back and up (S8: page dated 2025, section headed '2021 Changes'; S22 lists 2021 course updates). It played 396 yd at the 1991 U.S. Open (S7) and was the hardest hole at the 2002 PGA (S7). Wind off the lake is a major factor (S6, S27). Tournament setups: 2009 PGA Championship 402 (S15); 2016 Ryder Cup 402, played as Ryder Cup No. 7 (S12, S6); 2024 U.S. Amateur 400 (S19); 2026 KPMG Women's PGA 370 (S9). Women's handicap 16 (S2).

penalty_areas.description: Water left of the green, described as a lateral hazard (S7); the club's guide says two water hazards are in play (S6). The green is surrounded by bunkers and water (S5, S11).

green.features: Large, deep green with a pronounced bowl front-left and narrow shelves on the right and at the back (S5, S9, S11). Also described as two-tiered, with deep rough and bunkers long (S7); one of the most undulating greens on the course (S27).

holes.notes: Converted from a par 4 with a humpbacked fairway into a par 3 in the 1970s, with tees built where the fairway had been (Golf Digest dates it to 1979; S17, S23). Scott Simpson found the water in the 1991 U.S. Open playoff (S7). Fifth-hardest hole at the 2009 PGA (S7). Tournament setups: 2009 PGA Championship 182 (S15); 2016 Ryder Cup 186, played as Ryder Cup No. 8 (S12, S6); 2024 U.S. Amateur 184 (S19); 2026 KPMG Women's PGA 159 (S9). Women's handicap 18 (S2).

penalty_areas.description: No water or other penalty area is described on this hole by the club or the 2026 KPMG guide.

green.features: Three tiers, front to back (S5, S9, S15); a narrow front section (S13); a left bunker cuts into the green, with trees to the left (S9).

holes.notes: Bunkers on both sides of the fairway (S9, S11). A crest in the landing area hides a sideslope that kicks drives into the right rough (S17). A fairway bunker was removed for 2009; the left bunker from which Tiger Woods hit his 3-iron in 2002 was kept (S17). Fourth-hardest hole at both the 2002 and 2009 PGAs (S7). Tournament setups: 2009 PGA Championship 475 (S15); 2016 Ryder Cup 475, played as Ryder Cup No. 9 (S12, S6); 2024 U.S. Amateur 472 (S19); 2026 KPMG Women's PGA 412 (S9). Women's handicap 4 (S2).

gaps: Scorecard: Hazeltine publishes no scorecard online. Per-hole yardages come from Stymie (S1) and GolfPass (S2), which agree on every hole for the Tournament, Blue, Gold, White, Green and Black tees. They differ on Gold/White: S1 has 6,412 and S2 has 6,385 (Nos. 9 and 16). Neither page is dated. Blue/Gold (6,924) and White/Green (5,570) are listed only by S2, with no rating.

Older editions conflict: GolfLink (S3), 18Birdies (S4) and GolfPass's own tee table (S2) list Blue at 7,137, Gold at 6,665 and a 5,701 Red/Green tee, with different ratings. Stymie's set was used because its Tournament rating (77.8/148) matches the 2024 U.S. Amateur fact sheet (S19). The USGA NCRDB could not be queried (its search is a scripted form), so no tee rating is confirmed from the USGA directly.

Handicaps: men's indexes from S1 and S2 agree, and the club confirms No. 12 as the No. 2 handicap (S6). Women's indexes come from S2 only. 18Birdies (S4) lists a different, apparently older set, with No. 3 as the No. 1 handicap.

16th tee project: the club says the members' back tees on 16 were moved back and up (S8), but the page is dated 2025 under a '2021 Changes' heading, and it is unclear whether the card's 16th yardages (380 Blue, 352 Gold) reflect the change.

Elevation: the only number is for No. 10, a drop of more than 40 ft from mid-fairway to the green (S6), which is a lower bound and not tee-to-green. Nos. 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 12 and 18 have direction only. Nos. 4, 5, 7, 8, 11, 13, 14, 15, 16 and 17 have no tee-to-green direction. Site elevation is about 961 ft (USGS GNIS via S30).
Out of bounds: no local-rules sheet found. Only Nos. 5 (left) and 14 (right) have OB documented; all other holes are present = null.

Penalty areas: water locations are well documented, but red/yellow colour for daily play is not published; the only colour clues are from championship notes (S7). The brief's mention of Hazeltine Lake on No. 11 is not supported by any source.
Green size, depth and width: no per-hole or average figures found. The only measurement is No. 4's back shelf, about 10 yd deep (S9).
Green speed: no daily member Stimpmeter figure; only the 2024 U.S. Amateur expectation of 12.5-13.5 (S20). The current bentgrass variety is not named.
Hole names: none found; Hazeltine does not appear to name its holes.

Tournament data: the 2026 KPMG news article (S10) lists No. 6 at 402, which makes its total 6,782 instead of its stated 6,760; the KPMG course page (S9) has No. 6 at 380, summing to 6,760 (also on ESPN, S33), so S9 was used. The club's toughest-holes page (S7) captions No. 16 as a 572-yd par 5 for 2016, but that is Ryder Cup No. 16 (member No. 7). The 2016 Ryder Cup played member No. 17 at 186 against 182 on the card. Golf Channel (S16) gives the 2009 length as 7,685 in its text and 7,672 in a table; the per-hole card sums to 7,674. No per-hole yardages were found for the 2019 KPMG (listed at 6,807; S28) or the 1970 and 1991 U.S. Opens.
Location: OpenGolfAPI (S34) gives 44.736, -93.796, about 20 km south-west of the club. The USGS GNIS point (44.8278, -93.5828, S30) was used.
Blocked pages: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hazeltine_National_Golf_Club, the LPGA article on 2026 course preparation, and Golf Monthly's hole-11 guides could not be fetched (permission timeouts).
Women's par is not listed separately; par 72 is used for all tees.
